category_title: Students performing closed challenges through overt off-task social interaction
minimal_context: The student is participating in a daily competitive homework checking game where she needs to match a paragraph number to a main idea in her book.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's start our daily homework check game. Lisa, you are up for this round. Please read out loud which paragraph number on the right matches the main idea on the left for Item (b), 'Our five senses'.

STUDENT: (Turns to Brent, the male student sitting in front of me, and starts overtly talking to him)

TUTOR: Lisa, it is your turn for the game. Do you have the answer?

STUDENT: (Sam taps my hand and points to Item b in his book. I look down at my own book, but I do not look at Sam's pointing)

TUTOR: Lisa, we are waiting for you to read the paragraph number.

STUDENT: (Continues speaking with Brent, completely ignoring the fact that my name has been called for the game)

options.A: Provide an app that has instant rewards with audio and text for the game.
options.B: Intersperse requests to read only a sentence with requests to read a paragraph number.
options.C: Employ 'the look' to signal to the student a possible intervention.
options.D: Ensure the student is not rushed in making her contributions to the game.
